_readme: MONEY-1359 — request error rate on an APM service.
The zero-write family watches JOBS: did a scheduled run find work and write
nothing. Nothing watched whether the services answering those jobs, and the
user-facing API, were returning errors at all. This is the surviving scope of
the cancelled MONEY-452, trimmed to what the existing spans can support.
A RATIO, not a count. An absolute error count is a traffic measure wearing an
error's name: it rises on a busy morning and falls on a quiet night, so any
threshold that is quiet at 03:00 is deaf at 10:00. 5% of requests is the same
_no_latency_monitor_rationale: There is deliberately NO p95-latency sibling for stockbook-workers, and that
is a property of what its requests ARE rather than an omission.
Its HTTP requests are the JOBS. A Pub/Sub push handler runs until the job is
done, bounded by the 600s ack deadline, and several jobs deliberately use
most of it — xbrl-sync budgets 480s, stock-document-extract 420s. A p95 there
measures how much work the night had, not how healthy the service is, and an
alarm on it would fire on a busy backfill and stay quiet through an outage
that made every job exit early.
us-fundamentals DOES have a latency monitor and it is the right shape:
monitor-latency-p95.json watches detection freshness — SEC acceptance to our
row — which is a promise to a user rather than a measure of how much work
name: [{{env}}] {{service}} — request error rate over 5%
_default_zero_rationale: MONEY-1534. `default_zero()` wraps the NUMERATOR, and only the numerator.
A healthy service has NO errors series at all: the counter is written when
an error happens, never as a zero. Measured 2026-09-23 over 24h,
`trace.<span>.errors` returned no series for all four services here while
every `hits` series was live. The fill states 'no errors' as a real 0 in
the query instead of leaving a gap for the evaluator to interpret.
It is NOT what put monitor 22316281 in No Data, and it does not claim to
be. tiingo-realtime's errors series has never existed (20 days measured)
and its monitor 22319213 has read OK throughout, because the arithmetic
already treats an absent operand as 0 while the other side has points:
`errors / hits` returned zeros, not nothing. What vanished was the
DENOMINATOR (`web.request` renamed to `hono.request`), and a ratio over no
hits is no data. The fix for that is the span, declared once in
DD_SERVER_SPAN. The fill is kept because that implicit zero is observed
behaviour, not something this repo can pin.
NEVER around the denominator or the whole ratio. The grammar is
`time_aggr(window):space_aggr:metric{…}`; `default_zero()` wraps one
space-aggregated operand, and only the numerator's may be filled. Measured
on the dead span (query API, 1h): with no hits,
`default_zero(errors) / hits` is all-null, so the monitor goes No Data —
grey and visible, the state that surfaced this ticket. `default_zero(errors
/ hits)` is 181 zeros an hour: OK forever over a service nobody is
measuring, and this incident would never have been seen.
message:
More than 5% of {{service}} requests errored over the last 15 minutes.

APM: filter `service:{{service}} env:{{env}} status:error` and read the top RESOURCE. For stockbook-workers a resource is a job route (`/jobs/<name>`), so the job's own zero-write monitor and its `[job-outcome]` log line say what it actually did — this monitor tells you the route is failing, that one tells you whether anything was written.

A 500 here is a Pub/Sub RETRY, not a lost message: the failed delivery is redelivered up to 5 times and then parked on the dead-letter topic, which notifies separately. A sustained 5% is therefore work being done up to six times, not work being dropped.

@{{notify}}
_notify_no_data_rationale: FALSE, and for the reason monitor-latency-p95.json gives rather than the one
monitor-zero-write.json gives. A ratio over traffic has no points when there
is no traffic, and no traffic is a state we ship on purpose: the workers'
requests are scheduled jobs, so the small hours are legitimately empty, and
the api sees near-zero overnight IST.
Silence is watched by a DIFFERENT instrument — every scheduled job carries a
zero-write monitor whose counters are emitted from a `finally` on every run.
This monitor answers 'are requests FAILING'; those answer 'did the work
HAPPEN'. Restoring no-data here would page every quiet night and buy nothing.
_placeholders: {{service}}  APM service tag — stockbook-workers | us-fundamentals | tiingo-realtime | usemoney-market-data
{{span}}     the service's SERVER span, from DD_SERVER_SPAN in packages/datadog/src/constants.ts via dd_server_span — never typed into a row
